_comment: DO NOT EDIT: FILE GENERATED FOR PELICAN PANEL
name: mc-router
author: 50152835+s3tupw1zard@users.noreply.github.com
description: Routes Minecraft Java Edition connections to backend servers based on the requested hostname. Uses a Pelican-compatible multi-architecture image with mc-router preinstalled.

variables.name: Routes config
variables.description: Path to the JSON routes file. The recommended startup command watches this file for changes.

variables.name: Watch routes config
variables.description: Reload the routes file when it changes. Do not combine watched routes with MAPPING; a reload resets routes before re-reading the file.

variables.name: Mappings
variables.description: Optional comma- or newline-separated mappings such as play.example.com=10.0.0.10:25565. Intended for the Environment mappings startup command.

variables.name: Default backend
variables.description: Optional host:port used when no hostname mapping matches. For routes-file mode, prefer default-server in routes.json.

variables.name: Connection rate limit
variables.description: Maximum incoming connections per second. mc-router enforces a minimum of 1.

variables.name: Record logins
variables.description: Log player login information and make login metrics available to supported metrics backends.

variables.name: Send PROXY protocol
variables.description: Send PROXY protocol to backend servers. The backend must be configured to accept it.

variables.name: Receive PROXY protocol
variables.description: Expect PROXY protocol from the frontend proxy. Do not enable together with Dynamic PROXY protocol.

variables.name: Dynamic PROXY protocol
variables.description: Accept connections with or without PROXY protocol and forward received headers. Cannot be combined with send/receive PROXY protocol.

variables.name: Trusted proxies
variables.description: Optional comma-separated CIDR blocks trusted to provide PROXY headers, for example 10.0.0.0/8,100.64.0.0/10.

variables.name: Clients to allow
variables.description: Optional comma-separated client IPs or CIDRs to allow. When set, it takes precedence over the deny list.

variables.name: Clients to deny
variables.description: Optional comma-separated client IPs or CIDRs to deny.

variables.name: Timezone
variables.description: Timezone used for log timestamps, for example Europe/Berlin.
